I read the structure region by region, from left to right.

**Left end.** A methylsulfonyl group (CH3-SO2) sits on the nitrogen of a pyrrole. The pyrrole is substituted at position 3 with a C(=O)NH group, so the fragment is CS(=O)(=O)n1ccc(c1)C(=O)N.

**Glycine linker.** The pyrrole amide NH is bonded to CH2, then C(=O), then NH on the thiazole. This gives C(=O)NCC(=O)Nc1nc(cs1)...

**Thiazole to aryl rings.** The thiazole has S, C2 (bearing the NH), N, C4 (bearing the aryl group) and C5 (CH). C4 is attached to a benzene ring, which is meta-disubstituted. The other substituent on that benzene is the pyridine C4. The pyridine has its N at the bottom right and its C2 carrying the O, so the pyridine is c1cc(OCC...)ncc1.

**Linker.** From the pyridyl ether: O-CH2CH2-NH-C(=O)-CH2CH2-O-CH2CH2-O-CH2CH2-NH-Ar.

**Right end.** Ar is the isoindoline-1,3-dione with the NH at position 5. Its nitrogen carries the 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl group, which is drawn without stereochemistry.

**Assembly.**

CS(=O)(=O)n1ccc(c1)C(=O)NCC(=O)Nc1nc(cs1)-c1cccc(c1)-c1ccnc(OCCNC(=O)CCOCCOCCNc2ccc3C(=O)N(C4CCC(=O)NC4=O)C(=O)c3c2)c1

Checking the pyridine: c1ccnc(O...)c1 starts at C4 (attached to the aryl), then C5 and C6 (cc), then N, then C2 (bearing O), then C3 (c1). This is correct.

Checking the phthalimide: c2ccc3C(=O)N(...)C(=O)c3c2 starts at the NH-bearing carbon c2, then cc, then c3 (ring fusion) bearing C(=O), and closes through c3 and c2. The NH-bearing carbon is therefore bonded to the CH at the ring end, which is adjacent to the fusion carbon. That places it at position 5, as drawn.

SMILES: CS(=O)(=O)n1ccc(c1)C(=O)NCC(=O)Nc1nc(cs1)-c1cccc(c1)-c1ccnc(OCCNC(=O)CCOCCOCCNc2ccc3C(=O)N(C4CCC(=O)NC4=O)C(=O)c3c2)c1
